lines.en: Bia, you are twenty minutes late, and you look completely shocked. What on earth happened to you this morning?
lines.pt: Bia, você está vinte minutos atrasada e parece chocada. O que diabos aconteceu com você hoje de manhã?

lines.en: Let me tell you! I was walking to work when a dog suddenly jumped out of a taxi and ran away.
lines.pt: Deixa eu te contar! Eu estava indo a pé para o trabalho quando um cachorro de repente pulou de um táxi e fugiu.

lines.en: No way! Was the driver chasing it? I hope nobody got hurt while the dog was running across the road.
lines.pt: Não acredito! O motorista estava correndo atrás dele? Espero que ninguém tenha se machucado enquanto o cachorro cruzava a rua.

lines.en: Nobody did. The driver had just opened the door, so the dog escaped before he could grab the leash.
lines.pt: Ninguém se machucou. O motorista tinha acabado de abrir a porta, então o cachorro escapou antes que ele pegasse a guia.

lines.en: And what did you do? Knowing you, you did not stand there and watch the poor thing disappear.
lines.pt: E o que você fez? Conhecendo você, não ficou parada vendo o coitado desaparecer.

lines.en: I dropped my bag and ran after it. By the time I caught up, it had reached the park.
lines.pt: Larguei a bolsa e corri atrás dele. Quando o alcancei, ele já tinha chegado ao parque.

lines.en: Seriously? In that heat? And then what happened? Did you catch it, or did it keep running until you gave up?
lines.pt: Sério? Naquele calor? E aí, o que aconteceu? Você o pegou ou ele continuou correndo até você desistir?

lines.en: Just as I was about to give up, it stopped to drink from a fountain. I grabbed the leash.
lines.pt: Justo quando eu ia desistir, ele parou para beber água numa fonte. Eu peguei a guia.

lines.en: Brilliant! And the owner? After all that, I hope he said thank you, or at least bought you a coffee.
lines.pt: Genial! E o dono? Depois de tudo isso, espero que tenha agradecido ou pelo menos te pagado um café.

lines.en: He arrived later, out of breath and grateful. He had been looking for the dog since the taxi left.
lines.pt: Ele chegou depois, sem fôlego e agradecido. Estava procurando o cachorro desde que o táxi tinha ido embora.

lines.en: Well, that explains why you are late. Sit down, and the coffee is on me, you deserve it.
lines.pt: Bem, isso explica o atraso. Sente-se, o café é por minha conta, você merece.

facts.label: Contar uma história
facts.sub: Combine os tempos: I was walking when a dog suddenly jumped out. By the time I caught up, it had reached the park.

facts.label: Ação de fundo
facts.sub: Use was/were + -ing para a ação longa: I was walking to work. Depois entre com o passado simples para o fato que interrompe: when a dog suddenly jumped out. While liga duas ações longas ao mesmo tempo.

facts.label: Antes da história
facts.sub: Use had + particípio para o que já tinha acontecido: By the time I caught up, it had reached the park. O dono had been looking for the dog since the taxi left. Past perfect contínuo mostra uma busca que durou um tempo.

compare.ask: I was walking when a dog jumped out.
compare.br: No Brasil, dizemos “eu estava andando quando…” e “quando cheguei, já tinha…”.
compare.tip: Diga: “I was walking when a dog jumped out.”
compare.us: Em inglês: I was walking when… (passado contínuo + simples) e By the time I arrived, it had reached… (past perfect).

solo: Peça uma experiência pessoal do aluno com essa diferença.
group: Leia as duas colunas e peça que apontem a maior diferença.
Pergunta: I was walking when a dog jumped out.
extra90: Dupla: um fala como no Brasil, o outro como nos EUA.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: We use the past continuous for a background action.
We use past perfect for something before another past action.
items.why: Yes: it had reached the park.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: We use the past continuous for a background action. → Verdadeiro (Yes: I was walking.)
We use past perfect for something before another past action. → Verdadeiro (Yes: it had reached the park.)
“Suddenly” introduces an expected, slow event. → Falso (It introduces a sudden event.)

pages.title: A morning story · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a warm morning in a small café in Atlanta. Fay checks her watch twice. Her friend Bia is very late. At last the door opens. Bia walks in, red and out of breath. She has a story to tell.

“Bia, you are twenty minutes late, and you look completely shocked. What on earth happened to you this morning?” says Fay. “Let me tell you! I was walking to work when a dog suddenly jumped out of a taxi and ran away.” says Bia. “No way! Was the driver chasing it? I hope nobody got hurt while the dog was running across the road.” says Fay.
